_comment: Differentiation scaffolds playbook (Agent D). Maps KSSR performance levels (Tahap Penguasaan) to tier templates and generic scaffold moves. The Pedagogy Architect uses this to split the lesson's hands-on step into readiness tiers; the rule-based fallback builds tiers directly from these templates when no model is available.
intro_template: The hands-on and formative-check steps split into three readiness pathways, so every learner — from TP1 to TP6 — works at the right level on the same offline activity.
note: Tiers map to the KSSR performance levels (Tahap Penguasaan). No extra devices or internet are required for any tier — only printed scaffolds and peer grouping.

remedial: Provide visual vocabulary matching boards / picture-word cards for the key terms so tactile learners pair each item to its name before the main task.
Pair the student with a Core- or Enrichment-tier peer for any shared-device rotation; together they narrate one step aloud.
Reduce the formative check to fewer, picture-based questions instead of the full text set.
core: Run the baseline offline activity exactly as the plan describes.
Complete the full formative check, then explain one key idea to a partner in their own words.
enrichment: Act as peer-mentors during the device rotation, coaching a Remedial-tier classmate through the task.
Formulate alternative descriptors: write a short analogy comparing the concept to a familiar system.
Propose one additional challenge question to add to the class formative check.
